summary.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Shipbuilding order book ₹12,980 crore (~95% of total); P-17 Alpha ~₹4,519 crore, NGOPV ~₹3,075 crore, anti-submarine shallow water craft ~₹1,815 crore, Ocean Research Vessel ₹740 crore, Acoustic Research Ship ₹450 crore, Multipurpose Vessels plus Dredger ~₹1,355 crore.

segments.name: Bailey Bridge
segments.commentary: Order book ₹158 crore; management says 100% indigenous.

segments.name: Deck machinery
segments.commentary: Order book ₹58 crore; about 90% indigenous per management.

segments.name: Diesel engine plant
segments.commentary: Order book ₹82 crore; co-production with foreign OEM targeting 55-60% indigenization.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract expected to be signed in Q2 FY27; revenue recognition to start in FY28, with eighth ship completion around 2034-35.
Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.
Indigenisation: management says ~80-85% overall by value; weapons ~60%, survival ~70%, float (hull) 100% but ~10% of cost, propulsion engines not yet indigenous; large survey vessel >80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port revitalisation is about ₹200 crore over 18 months. Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the indigenisation level and where is GRSE still import-dependent?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall indigenisation is about 80-85% by value. Hull/float is 100% but about 10% of cost, weapons about 60%, survival about 70%, and diesel alternators 100%; propulsion engines are not yet indigenous. Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses and employee costs QoQ, and what is the pay commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Contract workforce cost is sinusoidal with delivery timing and will rise when a couple of ships deliver. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

risks_watch: NGC contract signing: already slipped from FY26-end and Q1; management guides Q2 FY27, and revenue recognition only starts in FY28.
Execution timing: P-17 Alpha large ship delivery targeted by November 2026, and the four remaining anti-submarine craft due in FY27; slippage would hit the quarterly run-rate.

Order book fell to ₹13,596 crore; conversion of the ~₹80,000 crore of live RFPs (120 fast interceptor craft, 31 water jet FACs, P-17 Bravo) and the ~₹70,000 crore expected RFPs (mine sounder vessels, LPDs) is key.
Expansion capex of about ₹4,400 crore (Raichak and Gujarat) with 3-5 year and ~3 year timelines; funding and approvals are still pending.
Bonus or stock split awaits direction from the administrative ministry and DIPAM; no timeline given.
Other expense and contract workforce costs are volatile with delivery phasing; watch whether Q2 FY27 margins hold with more deliveries.
key_quotes: We do not see any red flags with respect to the contract conclusion.
So, the current quarter's performance will be able to replicate in the coming quarters too.
It is for the first time in the last 10 years that our order book has dropped below ₹15,000 crore and I consider it the reflection of an excellent execution rate.
We are waiting for their instructions on this.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, order inflow and the expansion plan, with firm near-term guidance that Q1 performance is repeatable. More cautious on timing for the NGC contract (which has slipped), on indigenisation (which management says takes 5-10 years to reach 100%), and on corporate actions, which it deferred to the government.
